title: River Loft
description: Transformation of a historic warehouse into a light-filled residential loft, celebrating industrial heritage through material contrast.
longDescription: The River Loft project represents a careful negotiation between preservation and transformation. The 1920s warehouse structure — exposed brick, heavy timber columns, and expansive arched windows — became the organizing framework for a contemporary residence. Rather than concealing the building's industrial character, we amplified it through strategic insertions: a blackened steel staircase that floats between floors, walnut millwork that warmly contrasts the cool masonry, and a restrained material palette of concrete, glass, and oxidized metal. The result is a dialogue between eras, where each intervention respects the original while asserting its own time.

title: Meridian House
description: A hillside residence that frames the landscape through precise architectural gestures, blurring the boundary between interior and exterior.
longDescription: Perched on a steep hillside with panoramic city views, Meridian House redefines indoor-outdoor living through a series of framed apertures. The architecture operates as a lens — each window, door, and opening carefully composed to capture specific vistas while managing solar exposure. Deep overhangs, operable glass walls, and a material palette of board-formed concrete, ipe wood, and honed travertine create a seamless transition between conditioned and exterior spaces. The plan unfolds as a sequence of pavilions connected by covered walkways, allowing the landscape to penetrate the domestic realm.

title: Aurum Boutique Hotel
description: An intimate boutique hotel where brass, marble, and deep tones create a sense of collected luxury across 24 suites and public spaces.
longDescription: Aurum Boutique Hotel explores the concept of 'collected luxury' — spaces that feel curated over time rather than designed in a single gesture. The 24 suites and public areas unfold through a choreography of materials: brushed brass that catches and reflects light, verde alpi marble with its dramatic veining, deep walnut paneling, and custom textiles in jewel tones. Each suite is unique, yet unified by a consistent language of contrast. The lobby operates as a living room, with residential-scale seating, a curated library, and a brass-clad bar that glows at night. Public spaces encourage lingering through layered lighting, acoustic consideration, and tactile materials.

title: Apex Creative Office
description: A creative workplace that balances collaborative energy with focused work through spatial zoning and material warmth.
longDescription: Apex Creative Office reimagines the creative workplace as a series of distinct neighborhoods rather than an open plan. The 12,500 sq ft space is organized around a central 'spine' — a circulation artery that doubles as a gallery for rotating art installations. Radiating from this spine are zones calibrated for different work modes: deep-focus pods wrapped in sound-absorbing felt, collaborative studios with writable walls, a library for quiet research, and a social kitchen that anchors the culture. Material warmth — white oak, wool felt, terracotta — counters the typical tech-office sterility, while exposed mechanical systems and polished concrete maintain an honest, industrial character.

title: Terrace Residence
description: A historic mansion renovation that honors original detailing while introducing contemporary interventions.
longDescription: The Terrace Residence is a 1910 Prairie School mansion restored and reimagined for contemporary living. Our approach was surgical: preserve and restore all original millwork, stained glass, and plaster detailing while introducing modern systems and spatial flows. The kitchen — originally fragmented into service rooms — was opened to the garden through a new steel-and-glass addition that contrasts the historic brick. Primary suites gained spa-like baths clad in honed onyx and brass. Throughout, new interventions are expressed in a language of blackened steel and clear glass, making the dialogue between 1910 and 2022 legible and intentional.

title: Lumen Art Gallery
description: A flexible gallery space where controlled light and neutral surfaces create the ideal canvas for rotating contemporary exhibitions.
longDescription: Lumen Art Gallery was designed as a 'non-space' — a container that recedes to elevate the art within. The 8,000 sq ft column-free volume features a sawtooth north-light roof monitor that floods the space with consistent, glare-free daylight. Walls are finished in a proprietary ultra-matte plaster that eliminates reflection. A motorized scrim system allows precise control of natural light for light-sensitive works. The floor is polished concrete with integrated power and data grids for flexible installation. Even the HVAC is calibrated for minimal air velocity across wall surfaces. A lower level houses art storage, preparation, and a private viewing room for collectors.
